subject: Infra sprint GPU reallocation & autoscale-exemption request for Zephyr pilot
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Lim <sarah@zephyrlabs.com>
Date: 2027-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Infra sprint GPU reallocation & autoscale-exemption request for Zephyr pilot

Team —

We have a time-boxed ask from Zephyr Labs to run a latency-sensitive pilot that ships during our Oct infra sprint (target rollout window Oct 11–17). The pilot uses a new feature that increases peak concurrent connections and 95th percentile token throughput for a short period (approx. 48 hours of peak traffic).

Ask summary:
- Temporarily reallocate 20 GPU slots from low-priority dedicated pool "dev-labs-2" into a short-lived "zephyr-pilot" pool for Oct 11–18 (inclusive).
- Grant an autoscale-exemption for that pool so we can keep a minimum headroom of 20 slots during the pilot (prevents automatic scale-to-zero).

Why this is time-sensitive: the Zephyr pilot is an external demo tied to their commercial milestone; they requested the window during our infra sprint to validate the end-to-end latency improvements. We can limit customer impact if we pin the reallocation to that exact window and add safeguards.

Attached: realloc_proposal_Q4.xlsx (breakdown of affected reservations, projected token costs). Also linking a short MA plan draft: https://drive.redwood.com/file/d/1a2b3c-realloc-proposal

Immediate asks:
1) Ops: can you confirm whether the autoscale-exemption is operationally feasible for a temporary pool and what change controls are required? (hannah)
2) Sales: I need confirmation we won't violate any guaranteed reservations for paying customers and whether we should notify Zephyr of any reduced burst guarantees (marissa)
3) Eng: estimate net cost and rollback playbook (dev)

If we can get a quick go/no-go by EOD Oct 3 we can lock the schedule and run a canary on Oct 9.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

---
Attachment: realloc_proposal_Q4.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, Sarah Lim <sarah@zephyrlabs.com>
Date: 2027-10-01T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Infra sprint GPU reallocation & autoscale-exemption request for Zephyr pilot

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear write-up. A couple of red lines from commercial:
- Zephyr is on a reserved capacity contract for their production lane. We can consider cross-pooling for a pilot, but only if we don't reduce their contracted minimum during their production traffic windows.
- Any manual hold of autoscale behavior should be explicitly timeboxed and visible in the Console to prevent accidental double-dips by other teams.

Can you call out which reservations we plan to borrow from (pool names + customer reservations)? The attached workbook has anonymized rows — I need raw reservation ids to confirm impacts. Also please confirm whether Zephyr has been informed that this is a pilot-level carve (they expect identical SLAs to production otherwise).

If we proceed, Sales proposes the following operating constraints:
- Notify the customer with a one-paragraph advisory (ops & legal to approve).
- Keep a 4-hour rollback SLA during the pilot window.
- Billing: if we consume Zephyr's reserved capacity, account for adjustments in next month's invoice (finance will need a note).

Happy to jump on a quick call — I'm free Oct 2 afternoon.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

---

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Infra sprint GPU reallocation & autoscale-exemption request for Zephyr pilot

Jonas / team —

Operational notes after a quick runbook review:
- Temporary autoscale-exemption: feasible, but requires a one-line policy patch and a short maintenance window to stage the pool. I've sketched the diff (autoscale_policy_patch.diff) and included a fallback rule that forces graceful drain to a compatible spot if the underlying nodes drop below the threshold.
- Reservation impact: we can implement a "holdback" pattern — move 20 slots from a non-production dev pool (dev-labs-2) that currently has zero active reservations from paying customers. I will verify reservation ids and post them by EOD Oct 2.
- Monitoring: add a dedicated alert channel and a short-lived SLO override so on-call sees the elevated headroom.

Questions for engineering:
1) Dev — can you confirm the change to the autoscaler will not increase job latency for other pools? We need a latency regression run on a representative dataset by Oct 8.
2) Exact capacity numbers: the spreadsheet shows 20 GPUs; is that 20 full slots or 20 fractional equivalents (T4-style)? Please call out model variant assumptions.

I'll follow up with a change ticket (INFRA-2147) and include the policy diff. If you can confirm the exact reservations, I can schedule the maintenance window for Oct 10, 02:00–03:00 PT.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

---
Attachment: autoscale_policy_patch.diff (text, 2KB)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T14:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Infra sprint GPU reallocation & autoscale-exemption request for Zephyr pilot

On Fri, Oct 1, 2027 at 09:12, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
>
> We have a time-boxed ask from Zephyr Labs to run a latency-sensitive pilot that ships during our Oct infra sprint (target rollout window Oct 11–17).

Quick follow-up — engineering confirms:
- 20 GPU slots = 20 full GPU slots (NVIDIA A10-equivalent). Cost delta estimated at ~$9k for the 8-day window (projection in Jonas' workbook).
- Model variant: we'll run the pilot on the quantized v2-small variant to reduce per-token cost; performance tests show <6% latency difference vs baseline for Zephyr workload. I'll attach the perf run notes to the change ticket.
- Risk/rollback: if we see a 5%+ regression in median latency for other pools, we will stop the pilot and revert the hold within the 4-hour rollback SLA proposed by Marissa.

I can schedule the canary on Oct 9 (limited traffic to Zephyr test tenant) and full pilot Oct 11–18 as proposed. If Ops confirms reservation ids and legal signs off on the customer advisory, I consider this a green path.

Approving here: please reply-all with one-line approvals so I can attach them to INFRA-2147 and close the change window.

– Dev
Dev Patel
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
